2: 
3: ## 1. Problem Statement & Scope Boundaries
4: 
5: During autonomous multi-agent development sessions, operators have zero live visibility into running sessions, hierarchical sub-agent execution, or reasoning thought processes. Directly polling the active OpenCode SQLite database with default driver parameters risks contention, locking the database and causing running agent instances to fail with busy errors. Furthermore, multi-agent workflows frequently run multiple concurrent root sessions, each spawning specialized child sub-sessions (planner, coder, tester, reviewer).
6: 
7: Developers need an automated, non-locking SQLite database hook, an in-memory session tree reconstruction engine, a streamlined title-based ticket inference heuristic, and HTTP endpoints (REST and Server-Sent Events) to inspect live traces and tool failures. Relying on Git branch detection or workspace directory traversal is deliberately avoided because live sessions frequently execute inside detached worktrees where inspecting Git or filesystem state is undesirable and unreliable. If a ticket cannot be extracted directly from the session title, the system leaves the guessed ticket identifier empty, allowing users to override it manually in the UI. Crucially, all live trace telemetry must remain transient and in-memory, guaranteeing zero disk writes to workspaces or persistence ledgers.

1: # Contract: AL-17 Implement Non-Locking Live Database Hook, Session Tree Engine, Ticket Inference, and Live Trace Telemetry
2: 
3: ## 1. Problem Statement & Scope Boundaries
4: 
5: During autonomous multi-agent development sessions, operators have zero live visibility into running sessions, hierarchical sub-agent execution, or reasoning thought processes. Directly polling the active OpenCode SQLite database with default driver parameters risks contention, locking the database and causing running agent instances to fail with busy errors. Furthermore, multi-agent workflows frequently run multiple concurrent root sessions, each spawning specialized child sub-sessions (planner, coder, tester, reviewer).
6: 
7: Developers need an automated, non-locking SQLite database hook, an in-memory session tree reconstruction engine, a streamlined title-based ticket inference heuristic, and HTTP endpoints (REST and Server-Sent Events) to inspect live traces and tool failures. Relying on Git branch detection or workspace directory traversal is deliberately avoided because live sessions frequently execute inside detached worktrees where inspecting Git or filesystem state is undesirable and unreliable. If a ticket cannot be extracted directly from the session title, the system leaves the guessed ticket identifier empty, allowing users to override it manually in the UI. Crucially, all live trace telemetry must remain transient and in-memory, guaranteeing zero disk writes to workspaces or persistence ledgers.
8: 
9: ### In Scope
10: 1. Domain Functional Core (backend/internal/domain/live.go):
11:    - Pure domain models: LiveSessionNode, LiveSessionTree, LivePartFact, LiveMessageFact, and LiveTraceView.
12:    - Pure tool failure classifier: categorizes tool execution failures into severity tiers (high, medium, low, none) based on failure signatures, tracebacks, exit codes, and consecutive failure counts.
13:    - Pure session title ticket inference heuristic: inspects the session title exclusively, matches candidate ticket identifiers case-insensitively against configured ticket prefixes, and normalizes matches to canonical uppercase format (e.g. AL-17). Leaves the identifier empty (nil) with zero confidence when absent.
14:    - Pure tree hierarchy construction: groups root sessions and nests sub-sessions recursively based on parent-child relationships.
15: 2. Imperative Shell Adapters (backend/internal/adapters/live/):
16:    - Read-only SQLite hook opening connection with non-blocking pragmas: PRAGMA query_only = ON;, PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;, and PRAGMA read_uncommitted = ON; in WAL mode.
17:    - Session discovery querying active sessions updated within the configured window (live.active_threshold_seconds, default 300s) or with active execution states.

20:    - Live service coordinator with background polling timer (live.poll_interval_ms, default 2000ms) and pub/sub broadcaster for Server-Sent Events.
21: 3. HTTP Service Layer (backend/internal/adapters/http/):
22:    - GET /api/live/sessions: returns active LiveSessionTree with title-inferred tickets.
